gloss: light snowfall; fine snow; gently falling snow

definitions.gloss: light snowfall; fine snow; gently falling snow
definitions.explanation: Delicate, fine snow falling gently. A poetic and literary word evoking a quiet, beautiful winter scene.

examples.japanese: {細雪|ささめゆき}が{舞|ま}っている。
examples.english: Fine snow is dancing in the air.

examples.japanese: {窓|まど}の{外|そと}には{細雪|ささめゆき}が{静|しず}かに{降|ふ}っていた。
examples.english: Outside the window, fine snow was falling quietly.

examples.japanese: {夕暮|ゆうぐ}れの{街|まち}に{細雪|ささめゆき}が{降|ふ}り{始|はじ}め、{景色|けしき}が{一変|いっぺん}した。
examples.english: Fine snow began to fall on the town at dusk, transforming the scenery.

notes:
A literary and poetic word for delicate, gently falling snow. Composed of {細|ささめ} (fine, delicate) + {雪|ゆき} (snow). Evokes a quiet, elegant winter atmosphere and is associated with refined, literary Japanese.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {細雪|ささめゆき}が{舞|ま}う: fine snow dances in the air
- {細雪|ささめゆき}が{降|ふ}る: fine snow falls
- {細雪|ささめゆき}の{中|なか}: amid the gently falling snow

LITERARY NOTE:
The most famous use of this word is as the title of {谷崎潤一郎|たにざきじゅんいちろう}'s novel {細雪|ささめゆき} (The Makioka Sisters, 1943-1948), a masterwork of modern Japanese literature depicting the lives of four sisters in a wealthy Osaka family. The title evokes the beauty and transience of their fading world.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {粉雪|こなゆき}: powder snow — light, dry snow; less literary than {細雪|ささめゆき}
- {新雪|しんせつ}: fresh snow — emphasizes newness rather than delicacy
- {小雪|こゆき}: light snow — a more neutral term for light snowfall; also the name of a seasonal division in the traditional calendar
